title: Start system-problem investigations from a chat command
summary: PostNL's AI team built a Slack command that has AWS DevOps Agent investigate system problems, so on-call engineers spend less time gathering evidence while keeping the decisions.
agent_role: The agent does the first investigation pass using logs, metrics and topology and posts findings to a Slack thread; engineers interpret the findings and decide next steps.
outcome: The author says the agent took on the first investigation pass while engineers kept ownership of interpretation and next steps; no figures are reported.
what_they_did: PostNL's AI team set up AWS DevOps Agent with limited access permissions. Engineers type a Slack command such as '/watchdog investigate the 429s we are seeing'. That kicks off an investigation of the system's logs, performance numbers and how its parts connect. The findings come back in the same Slack thread.
how_it_went: The author says the agent now does the first round of investigation. On-call engineers spend less time collecting evidence and still decide what it means and what to do. No figures are given.
worth_knowing: Much of the setup could be written as code, but the agent's skills still had to be set up by hand in Amazon's web console at the time.
prompt: Help me set up an incident-investigation workflow: when I post '/investigate [symptom]' in [Slack channel], gather evidence from [our logs and metrics source], recent deployments and service dependencies for [service], then post a hypothesis with supporting evidence to the thread. Use only read-only access scoped to [account or resources]. Show me the architecture and permissions plan first and wait for my approval before deploying anything.

curation.rationale: A real team deployment with architecture and CDK code showing how incident investigation was wired into Slack, but no measured results are given.
